<!-- README.md -->

# Linecaster

### Modular OCR pipelines you can run anywhere

<p align="center">
  <img src="docs/linecaster.png" alt="Line drawing of an Intertype C4 linecaster, a hot-metal typesetting machine" width="353">
</p>
<p align="center"><sub>An Intertype C4 linecaster (1961), after a photograph in the Science Museum Group
Collection, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. <a href="#license">Credit</a></sub></p>

Linecaster turns page images into text, with any OCR model, on any machine, and tells you how good the result is.

## The problem

There are dozens of good OCR models: classic engines that read line by line, and vision-language models that read
a whole page. Each comes with its own installation, its own input and output formats and its own scripts. That
makes four things harder than they should be:

- **Trying another model** means writing new glue code, so most projects stay with the first model that worked.
- **Combining models**, such as one model's layout with another model's text recognition, is not possible at all
  with most tools.
- **Going from ten pages to ten million** means rewriting the same job for a cluster.
- **Knowing which setup is best** for your material needs ground truth and a fair comparison, which few tools
  include.

Linecaster puts every model behind the same few options and every result into the same record. You change a
model by changing one word, you run the same pipeline on a laptop or a cluster, and you score the result against
ground truth.

<p align="center">
  <img src="docs/pipeline.svg" alt="Page images are read either by one vision-language model that reads the whole page, or by one model for each step: layout, lines, text, tables, headings and paragraphs. Both write page records, from which Markdown, HTML and other files are written." width="900">
</p>

## What it does

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| 📥 | **Harvest** | Fetch page images from IIIF and METS manifests, with rate limits, proxies and resume |
| 🖼️ | **Convert** | Convert page images to JPEG, JPEG 2000, PNG or WebP, on the GPU where there is one |
| 🤖 | **Read with a vision-language model** | Models that read a whole page in one go, served by [vLLM] or [SGLang] |
| 🧩 | **Read step by step** | Layout, lines, text, tables and formulas, each by a model you pick: [PaddleX], [kraken], [Tesseract] |
| 🧱 | **Structure** | Headings and their levels, paragraphs, and a document per page |
| 📚 | **Bind** | Join pages into books and issues, with one text per item |
| 📝 | **Write** | Markdown, HTML, plain text and JSON; [ALTO], [PAGE-XML] and [hOCR] with every word's position |
| 🔤 | **Keep the text as read** | The stored text is exactly what the model read; every change is a rule you name |
| 🎓 | **Import ground truth** | ALTO, PAGE-XML, hOCR, TEI, HTML and plain text, read into the same records |
| 🎯 | **Score** | Character and word error rates with confidence intervals, for pages, tables and formulas |
| 🌍 | **Run anywhere** | A laptop, a GPU server, Ray, Slurm or [Hugging Face Jobs][HF Jobs]: the pipeline stays the same |
| 🔁 | **Survive long runs** | An interrupted run resumes; a page that fails is set aside with the reason |
| 🔎 | **Trace everything** | Each result names the model that made it; each run records its models, settings and versions |

**Documentation:** [storytracer.github.io/linecaster](https://storytracer.github.io/linecaster/)

## Quick start

You need Python 3.12 and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) 0.13.6 or newer. An NVIDIA GPU is recommended.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/storytracer/linecaster
cd linecaster
```

There is nothing to install. Every pipeline is a [uv script][uv scripts] with pinned dependencies, which `uv run`
installs on the first run. Models download on first use.

The three examples below go from simple to flexible: one model for the whole page, a model for each step, and a
tested combination under a name.

## 1. One model reads the page

A vision-language model reads a whole page in one request, so there is one model to pick. It runs behind [vLLM]
or [SGLang], which needs an NVIDIA GPU and the `vllm` command on the `PATH`:

```bash
uv run pipelines/transcribe_vlm.py scans/ out/ --recognition lightonocr-2-1b
```

This reads the images in `scans/` and writes:

| In `out/` | What it is |
|---|---|
| `pages/` | one page record per page: the text the model read, with the model's raw answer |
| `rejects/` | pages that failed, each with the reason |
| `run.yaml` | the run record: what ran, with which models and versions |

`uv run linecaster presets --step recognition` lists the models. Tutorial:
[Run a vision-language model](docs/start/vlm.md).

## 2. A model for each step

The modular pipeline divides the work into steps, and each option names a **preset**: a model at a pinned
revision with its settings.

```bash
uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py scans/ out/ \
  --layout pp-doclayoutv3 \
  --lines pp-ocrv6-medium-det \
  --recognition paddlex-ppocrv6-medium \
  --document linked-document \
  --files out/files --formats md,html
```

This also writes a Markdown and an HTML file for each page to `out/files/`.

To swap a model, change one option. This run keeps the layout and the lines and reads the text with Tesseract:

```bash
uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py scans/ out-tesseract/ \
  --layout pp-doclayoutv3 \
  --lines pp-ocrv6-medium-det \
  --recognition tesseract-best-latin \
  --document linked-document \
  --files out-tesseract/files --formats md,html
```

More steps are more options:

| Option | Step |
|---|---|
| `--layout` | the regions of a page and their order (`single-region`: the whole page, no layout model) |
| `--lines` | the lines |
| `--recognition` | the text of each line |
| `--tables` | table cells |
| `--formulas` | formulas as LaTeX (its model needs torch: run it in a script that installs torch, as a recipe's does) |
| `--hierarchy` | headings and their levels |
| `--paragraphs` | lines joined into paragraphs |
| `--document` | the page as a document, which Markdown, HTML and JSON are written from |

No step has a default, so a run always names what it ran. `--set recognition.batch_size=4` changes one setting
of a preset, `--dry-run` prints the plan and runs nothing, and `--help` lists everything else.

Tutorial: [Combine models step by step](docs/start/first-run.md).

### The same in Python

A `Pipeline` is a list of components, one for each thing that happens to a page. Save this as a script and run
it with `uv run`:

```python
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.12,<3.13"
# dependencies = ["linecaster", "linecaster-paddlex"]
#
# [tool.uv.sources]
# linecaster = { git = "https://github.com/storytracer/linecaster", branch = "main" }
# linecaster-paddlex = { git = "https://github.com/storytracer/linecaster", branch = "main", subdirectory = "engines/paddlex" }
# ///
from linecaster import Pipeline
from linecaster.components.document import DocumentComposer
from linecaster.components.hierarchy import HierarchyDetector
from linecaster.components.layout import LayoutDetector
from linecaster.components.lines import LineAssigner, LineDetector
from linecaster.components.paragraphs import ParagraphBuilder
from linecaster.components.readers import ImageFolderReader
from linecaster.components.recognition import LineRecognizer
from linecaster.components.writers import PageFileWriter, PageJsonlWriter

pipeline = Pipeline([
    ImageFolderReader("scans/"),
    LayoutDetector("pp-doclayoutv3"),
    LineDetector("pp-ocrv6-medium-det"),
    LineAssigner(),
    LineRecognizer("paddlex-ppocrv6-medium"),
    HierarchyDetector("ratios"),
    ParagraphBuilder("unicode-paragraphs"),
    DocumentComposer("linked-document"),
    PageJsonlWriter("out/pages"),
    PageFileWriter("out/files", formats=("md", "html")),
])
pipeline.run("out")
```

Every component declares what it reads and what it adds. `run` checks these declarations first, so a pipeline
that cannot work stops before it starts: a recognizer without a line detector fails at once, with the reason.
`pipeline.draw()` gives the pipeline's graph, and `pipeline.to_dict()` the pipeline as plain data.

Tutorial: [A pipeline in Python](docs/start/python.md).

## 3. A recipe

A **recipe** is a tested combination kept under a name: one preset for each step, and the texts to write. A
recipe has a script of its own with exactly the engines it needs, and `launch.py` runs it by name:

```bash
uv run launch.py                          # list the recipes
uv run launch.py squiddle scans/ out/     # run one
```

Options after the name replace single steps, and the run record lists what was changed. A recipe's script also
runs from its URL, without a checkout:

```bash
uv run https://raw.githubusercontent.com/storytracer/linecaster/main/recipes/squiddle.py scans/ out/
```

## Input and output

| Pages from | Options |
|---|---|
| a folder of images | `IMAGES` (with `--item-from-parent`, each subfolder is an item) |
| a list of images | `IMAGES --paths-file pages.txt` |
| Parquet with an image column | `--parquet PATH` |
| IIIF or METS manifests | `--manifests FOLDER`, or a list or a Parquet table of their URLs |
| an earlier run | `--pages OUT/pages` |

Paths can be local or remote: `s3://`, `hf://`, `http(s)://` and every other [fsspec] protocol.

| Output | Option |
|---|---|
| page records, as JSON Lines or Parquet | always, in `OUT/pages/` |
| Markdown, HTML, plain text and JSON per page | `--files DIR --formats md,html,txt,json`, with `--document` |
| ALTO, PAGE-XML and hOCR, with every word's position | `--files DIR --formats alto,page,hocr` |
| one text per book or issue | `--item-texts DIR --text literal:txt`, with `--document` |

The stored text is exactly what the model read. Joining divided words, folding historic letterforms and similar
changes are made only in a text you ask for, by rules you name: `--text latin-historic+flow:md`.
[Text and normalization](docs/concepts/text.md) explains why.

## Run anywhere

| Where | Options |
|---|---|
| this machine | none: the models load inside the pipeline |
| this machine, with a model server | `--backend served` |
| a Ray cluster | `--on ray --tasks 64` |
| Hugging Face Jobs | `--on hf-jobs --namespace NS --commit <sha>` |
| a Slurm cluster | from Python, with [datatrove]'s Slurm executor |

Linecaster builds on [datatrove], which divides the pages into tasks and resumes a run where it stopped.
[Running at scale](docs/reference/running.md) has the setup for each of these, and for collections that are
fetched first and transcribed later.

## Score a run

Ground truth is read into the same page records as a run's output, so the two can be compared:

```bash
uv run pipelines/import_transcriptions.py truth/ --parquet ocr.parquet --data-key alto --importer alto-import
uv run linecaster benchmark init truth/pages benchmark.yaml
uv run linecaster score out/ truth/pages --benchmark benchmark.yaml
```

The result is an evidence record: error rates with their confidence intervals, and exactly how they were
measured. Tutorial: [Score a run against ground truth](docs/start/score.md).

## How it works

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| component | does one thing to a page: finds the lines, reads them, writes a file |
| step | one kind of work: `layout`, `lines`, `recognition`, `tables`, `formulas`, `hierarchy`, `paragraphs`, `document` |
| engine | the code that runs a model: one package per OCR library (`linecaster-paddlex`, `linecaster-kraken`, `linecaster-tesseract`, ...) |
| preset | an engine, a model at a pinned revision and settings, under one name; what you pick for a step |
| recipe | a tested set of presets, one for each step |
| page record | everything the components found on one page, each finding with the model that made it |
| run record | what a run ran: every preset with its hash, and the versions |

A component adds to the page record and never overwrites what is there. Files and texts are written from the
record, so one run can serve Markdown to a reader and ALTO to a library. The
[overview](docs/concepts/overview.md) explains these ideas in a few minutes.

<!-- docs/start/vlm.md -->

# Run a vision-language model

A vision-language model (VLM) reads a whole page in one request and returns its text, often with layout and
tables. This tutorial runs one on a folder of page images.

## What you need

- Python 3.12 and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) 0.13.6 or newer
- a folder of page images, here `scans/`
- an NVIDIA GPU
- the `vllm` command on your `PATH`, or let linecaster build an environment for it with uv

## 1. Get linecaster

```bash
git clone https://github.com/storytracer/linecaster
cd linecaster
```

There is nothing to install: every pipeline is a uv script that brings its own environment on its first run.

## 2. Pick a preset

```bash
uv run linecaster presets --step recognition
```

A **preset** is a model with its settings. The presets whose engine is `chat.v1` are vision-language models, for
example `lightonocr-2-1b`.

## 3. Run it

The pipeline has one step to fill:

```bash
uv run pipelines/transcribe_vlm.py scans/ out/ --recognition lightonocr-2-1b
```

Linecaster starts a vLLM server for the model, sends the pages to it and stops the server when the run ends.
Starting the server takes a few minutes. `uv run launch.py lightonocr-2-1b scans/ out/` is a shorter way to write
the same run.

## 4. Use a server that is already running

If you already serve the model, name its address and no server is started:

```bash
uv run pipelines/transcribe_vlm.py scans/ out/ --recognition lightonocr-2-1b \
  --recognition-endpoint http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1
```

## 5. Let a layout model find the regions first

Some presets read one layout region at a time. Add a layout preset, and the model reads each region:

```bash
uv run pipelines/transcribe_vlm.py scans/ out/ --layout pp-doclayoutv3 --recognition minicpm-ocr-1.0
```

## What is in the page record

The model's answer is kept verbatim as a **raw output**, next to the regions, lines and text that linecaster
parsed from it. If a page looks wrong, the raw output shows what the model actually wrote.

## Next

- [Combine models step by step](first-run.md): a model for each step instead of one for the page.
- [Score a run against ground truth](score.md).
- The [catalog](../catalog/README.md) has a page for every preset, with the model's settings.

<!-- docs/start/first-run.md -->

# Combine models step by step

This tutorial transcribes a folder of page images with the modular pipeline. You choose a model for each step on
the command line, then swap one of them for another.

## What you need

- Python 3.12 and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) 0.13.6 or newer
- a folder of page images, here `scans/`

An NVIDIA GPU is recommended: the models run much faster on one.

## 1. Get linecaster

```bash
git clone https://github.com/storytracer/linecaster
cd linecaster
```

There is nothing to install: every pipeline is a uv script that brings its own environment on its first run.
If you followed [Run a vision-language model](vlm.md), you have it already.

## 2. See what you can combine

The modular pipeline works in **steps**: a layout model finds the regions of a page, a line detector finds the
lines, and a line recognizer reads each line. For every step you pick a **preset**: a model with its settings.

```bash
uv run linecaster presets --step layout
uv run linecaster presets --step lines
uv run linecaster presets --step recognition
```

Each command lists the presets of one step, with their engine, model and license.

## 3. Run it

Name one preset for each step:

```bash
uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py scans/ out/ \
  --layout pp-doclayoutv3 \
  --lines pp-ocrv6-medium-det \
  --recognition paddlex-ppocrv6-medium
```

The first run installs the engines and downloads the models. No step has a default, so the command line says
exactly what ran.

## 4. Look at the result

| In `out/` | What it is |
|---|---|
| `pages/` | one page record per page: everything that was found, with who found it |
| `rejects/` | pages that failed, each with the reason |
| `run.yaml` | the run record: what ran, with which presets and versions |

To get files you can open, add the document step, a folder and the formats:

```bash
uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py scans/ out/ \
  --layout pp-doclayoutv3 --lines pp-ocrv6-medium-det --recognition paddlex-ppocrv6-medium \
  --document linked-document \
  --files out/files --formats md,html
```

This writes a Markdown and an HTML file for each page. The run resumes: pages that are already done are not read
again.

## 5. Swap one model

Every step is independent of the others. This run keeps the layout and the lines and reads the text with
Tesseract instead:

```bash
uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py scans/ out-tesseract/ \
  --layout pp-doclayoutv3 --lines pp-ocrv6-medium-det \
  --recognition tesseract-best-latin \
  --document linked-document \
  --files out-tesseract/files --formats md,html
```

Compare the two folders of Markdown files to see what the change did.

## 6. Add steps

More steps are more options. This run also reads tables, finds the headings and joins the lines into paragraphs:

```bash
uv run pipelines/transcribe_modular.py scans/ out-full/ \
  --layout pp-doclayoutv3 --lines pp-ocrv6-medium-det --recognition paddlex-ppocrv6-medium \
  --tables slanet-plus \
  --hierarchy ratios --paragraphs unicode-paragraphs --document linked-document \
  --files out-full/files --formats md,html
```

Two more options are useful while you try things out:

| Option | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | prints the plan and its graph, and runs nothing |
| `--set recognition.batch_size=4` | changes one option of a step's preset |

`--help` lists every option.

## 7. Run a recipe

Once a combination works for your material, it can be kept as a **recipe**: a named, tested set of presets, one
for each step. Linecaster's catalog has the recipe `squiddle`, and `launch.py` runs a recipe by its name:

```bash
uv run launch.py squiddle scans/ out-squiddle/
```

A recipe has a script of its own with exactly the engines its presets need. `squiddle` also reads formulas, with a
model that needs torch, which `transcribe_modular.py` does not install.

Options after the recipe's name replace single steps, and the run record lists what you changed.

## Next

- [Build the same pipeline in Python](python.md).
- Read the [overview](../concepts/overview.md) to see how the parts fit together.

<!-- docs/start/python.md -->

# A pipeline in Python

This tutorial builds the pipeline of [Combine models step by step](first-run.md) in Python: a list of components that
you can check, draw, run and change.

## What you need

- Python 3.12 and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) 0.13.6 or newer
- a folder of page images, here `scans/`

## 1. Write the script

Save this as `my_pipeline.py`. The comment at the top tells uv which packages the script needs: linecaster and
the engine packages of the models it names.

```python
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.12,<3.13"
# dependencies = ["linecaster", "linecaster-paddlex", "linecaster-tesseract"]
#
# [tool.uv.sources]
# linecaster = { git = "https://github.com/storytracer/linecaster", branch = "main" }
# linecaster-paddlex = { git = "https://github.com/storytracer/linecaster", branch = "main", subdirectory = "engines/paddlex" }
# linecaster-tesseract = { git = "https://github.com/storytracer/linecaster", branch = "main", subdirectory = "engines/tesseract" }
# ///
from linecaster import Pipeline
from linecaster.components.document import DocumentComposer
from linecaster.components.layout import LayoutDetector
from linecaster.components.lines import LineAssigner, LineDetector
from linecaster.components.readers import ImageFolderReader
from linecaster.components.recognition import LineRecognizer
from linecaster.components.writers import PageFileWriter, PageJsonlWriter

pipeline = Pipeline([
    ImageFolderReader("scans/"),
    LayoutDetector("pp-doclayoutv3"),
    LineDetector("pp-ocrv6-medium-det"),
    LineAssigner(),
    LineRecognizer("paddlex-ppocrv6-medium"),
    DocumentComposer("linked-document"),
    PageJsonlWriter("out/pages"),
    PageFileWriter("out/files", formats=("md", "html")),
])
pipeline.run("out")
```

A **component** does one thing to a page. A model component takes a **preset** by its id, the same ids as on the
command line. `LineAssigner` needs no model: it says which region each line belongs to. `DocumentComposer` builds the page's
document, which the Markdown and HTML files are written from.

## 2. Run it

```bash
uv run my_pipeline.py
```

The page records are in `out/pages/` and the Markdown and HTML files in `out/files/`.

## 3. Swap one component's model

Change one line and run the script again with another output folder:

```python
    LineRecognizer("tesseract-best-latin"),
```

Nothing else changes: the recognizer reads the lines, whoever found them.

## 4. Check a pipeline before it runs

Every component declares what it reads and what it adds. `check()` compares these declarations for the whole
list, and `run()` calls it first. A recognizer without a line detector fails at once:

```python
Pipeline([
    ImageFolderReader("scans/"),
    LineRecognizer("paddlex-ppocrv6-medium"),
    PageJsonlWriter("out/pages"),
]).check()
```

```text
PipelineConfigError: the pipeline cannot run:
- LineRecognizer (recognition (in-process)) reads ocr_new:lines, which no component before it in the pipeline adds
```

`print(pipeline.draw())` prints the pipeline's graph as a Mermaid diagram: which component reads what from which.

## 5. Add components

Components for headings and paragraphs go after the recognizer, before the document:

```python
from linecaster.components.hierarchy import HierarchyDetector
from linecaster.components.paragraphs import ParagraphBuilder

pipeline = Pipeline([
    ImageFolderReader("scans/"),
    LayoutDetector("pp-doclayoutv3"),
    LineDetector("pp-ocrv6-medium-det"),
    LineAssigner(),
    LineRecognizer("paddlex-ppocrv6-medium"),
    HierarchyDetector("ratios"),
    ParagraphBuilder("unicode-paragraphs"),
    DocumentComposer("linked-document"),
    PageJsonlWriter("out/pages"),
    PageFileWriter("out/files", formats=("md", "html")),
])
```

## 6. Keep a pipeline as data

`pipeline.to_dict()` gives the pipeline as plain data, and `Pipeline.from_dict()` builds it again. The data names
every component with its options and every preset with its hash.

## Next

- [Components and pipelines](../concepts/pipelines.md) explains components, contracts and backends.
- The [components reference](../components/README.md) has a page for each component.
- [Running at scale](../reference/running.md): the same pipeline on a cluster.

<!-- docs/start/score.md -->

# Score a run against ground truth

This tutorial measures how well a run read its pages. You need a run (see [Combine models step by step](first-run.md)) and
ground truth for the same pages: transcriptions made or checked by people.

## 1. Import the ground truth

Linecaster scores page records against page records, so the ground truth is imported first. Here the ground
truth is a Parquet table with one row per page and the page's ALTO file in the column `alto`:

```bash
uv run pipelines/import_transcriptions.py truth/ --parquet ocr.parquet --data-key alto --importer alto-import
```

The page records are in `truth/pages`. Other importers read PAGE-XML, hOCR, TEI, HTML and plain text;
`linecaster presets --step import` lists them.

## 2. Check it

```bash
linecaster ground-truth check truth/pages
```

This reports what the ground truth holds: how many pages, lines, tables and formulas, in which languages.

## 3. Write a benchmark

A benchmark says how to score: which pages, which comparison and which metrics. This writes one that fits the
ground truth:

```bash
linecaster benchmark init truth/pages benchmark.yaml
```

Open `benchmark.yaml` and read it. It is short, and every choice in it is yours to change.

## 4. Score the run

```bash
linecaster score out/ truth/pages --benchmark benchmark.yaml
```

The results are in `out/scores/`:

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `scores.parquet` | the counts for every page |
| `evidence.yaml` | the summary: error rates with their confidence intervals, and exactly how they were measured |

## 5. Compare two runs

Score a second run with the same benchmark. Two evidence records with the same benchmark were measured the same
way, so their numbers can be compared.

## Next

- [Evaluation](../concepts/evaluation.md) explains the parts.
- The [evaluation reference](../reference/evaluation.md) defines every metric.

<!-- docs/concepts/overview.md -->

# Overview

Linecaster turns page images into text. This page explains its few main ideas and how they fit together. Each idea
has a page of its own, and the [glossary](../reference/glossary.md) lists every term.

## A pipeline of components

A **pipeline** is an ordered list of **components**. Pages go through it one after another, and each component
reads a page and adds something to it.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    R[reader] --> L[layout] --> D[lines] --> T[recognition] --> H[hierarchy] --> P[paragraphs] --> C[document] --> W[writers]
```

This is the modular pipeline: a layout model finds the regions of a page, a line detector finds the lines, and a
line recognizer reads each line. Rule-based components then find the headings, join the lines into paragraphs and
build a document. A second kind of pipeline is shorter: a vision-language model reads the whole page in one go.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    R[reader] --> V[recognition by a VLM] --> W[writers]
```

Each box is a **step**: one kind of work. What does the work at a step is your choice.

Read more: [components and pipelines](pipelines.md).

## Models, engines and presets

Three things work together at a step:

- A **model** is a file of weights from upstream, pinned to an exact revision.
- An **engine** is the code that loads a model and runs it. Rule-based engines need no model.
- A **preset** is a named configuration of one engine with one model. A preset is what you pick:
  `--recognition kraken-ppocrv6-medium`.

A **recipe** is a tested combination of presets, one for each step. All of these are listed in the **catalog**.

Read more: [models, engines and presets](models.md).

## The page record

A pipeline's result is one **page record** per page. It holds everything every component said about the page: the
regions, the lines, the text of each line, the tables, and who said it. Nothing in it is overwritten.

The text in the record is exactly what the model read. Changes such as joining hyphenated words are made only when
you ask for a text to be written, by a **strategy** you name.

Read more: [page records](page-records.md) and [text and normalization](text.md).

## Running anywhere

Linecaster builds on [datatrove](https://github.com/huggingface/datatrove), which runs a pipeline on a laptop, on
a Ray cluster or on Hugging Face Jobs. The pipeline stays the same; only the command line changes. A run can be
interrupted and resumed, and a page that fails is set aside with the reason.

## Ground truth and scoring

Linecaster also reads **ground truth** (transcriptions made by people) in many formats into the same page records,
and scores a run against it.

Read more: [evaluation](evaluation.md).

## Where to go next

- [Run a vision-language model](../start/vlm.md): one model reads the page.
- [Combine models step by step](../start/first-run.md): a model for each step, on the command line.
- [A pipeline in Python](../start/python.md).
- [Score a run against ground truth](../start/score.md).

<!-- docs/concepts/pipelines.md -->

# Components and pipelines

## Components

A component does one thing to a page: it finds the lines, reads them, or writes a file. Technically it is a
datatrove `PipelineStep`. Components are named after what they do.

| Step | Components | What they add |
|---|---|---|
| reading input | `ImageFolderReader`, `ImageParquetReader`, `ManifestReader`, `PdfReader`, `PageRecordReader` | the page and its image |
| `layout` | `LayoutDetector` | regions and their reading order |
| `lines` | `LineDetector`, `LineAssigner` | lines, and which region each belongs to |
| `recognition` | `LineRecognizer`, `PageRecognizer`, `RegionRecognizer` | the text |
| `tables`, `formulas` | `TableRecognizer`, `FormulaRecognizer` | table cells, LaTeX |
| `hierarchy` | `HierarchyDetector` | heading levels |
| `paragraphs` | `ParagraphBuilder` | paragraphs |
| `document` | `DocumentComposer` | the document |
| writing output | `PageJsonlWriter`, `PageParquetWriter`, `PageFileWriter`, `ItemTextWriter`, ... | files |

The [components reference](../components/README.md) has a page for each.

## Contracts

Every component declares a **contract**: which parts of the page record it reads and which it adds. A
`LineRecognizer` reads the image and the lines, and adds the text.

Before a run starts, linecaster checks the contracts of the whole pipeline. If a component reads something that no
earlier component adds, the run does not start and the message says what is missing.

## Writing a pipeline

A `Pipeline` is a list of components:

```python
from linecaster import Pipeline
from linecaster.components.layout import LayoutDetector
from linecaster.components.lines import LineAssigner, LineDetector
from linecaster.components.readers import ImageFolderReader
from linecaster.components.recognition import LineRecognizer
from linecaster.components.writers import PageJsonlWriter

pipeline = Pipeline([
    ImageFolderReader("scans/"),
    LayoutDetector("pp-doclayoutv3"),
    LineDetector("pp-ocrv6-medium-det"),
    LineAssigner(),
    LineRecognizer("kraken-ppocrv6-medium"),
    PageJsonlWriter("out/pages"),
])
pipeline.check()        # the contracts, before anything runs
pipeline.run("out")     # on this machine
```

A model component takes a preset by its id. `check()` returns a plan of stages, and each stage is a list that any
datatrove executor runs: `pipeline.run()` uses the local one. `pipeline.to_dict()` gives the pipeline as plain
data, and `Pipeline.from_dict()` builds it again.

## Pipeline templates and scripts

Most people do not write the list themselves. A **pipeline template** builds a common kind of pipeline from
command-line options, and a **pipeline script** in `pipelines/` runs one template in its own environment:

| Script | Builds |
|---|---|
| `transcribe_modular.py` | layout, lines, a line recognizer, then hierarchy, paragraphs and the document |
| `transcribe_vlm.py` | a vision-language model per page, or per layout region |
| `transcribe_page.py` | a page engine per page |
| `harvest.py` | downloads page images from manifests |
| `bind.py` | item texts and item documents from page records |
| `convert.py` | converts page images |
| `import_transcriptions.py` | reads transcriptions in any format into page records |
| `score.py` | scores a run against a ground truth |

A template has a **slot** for each step, and you fill a slot with a preset: `--layout pp-doclayoutv3`. No slot has
a default. A **recipe** fills all slots at once.

## Where a model runs

A model component runs its engine in one of three places, its **backend**:

- in the pipeline's own process,
- behind `linecaster serve`, a server that hosts engines,
- behind an OpenAI-compatible server such as vLLM, for vision-language models.

The result is the same in all three: a request carries one page, and a page's result depends only on that page.

## Reference

[Pipelines](../reference/pipelines.md) has the details: contracts, checks, failures, the run record, samples.

<!-- docs/concepts/models.md -->

# Models, engines and presets

A preset names the model that does a step's work, and the catalog lists the presets you can pick.

## The three parts

| Part | What it is | Example |
|---|---|---|
| model | weights from upstream, pinned to a revision and checked by hash | `kraken-ppocrv6-medium` |
| engine | code that loads a model and processes one unit per call | `kraken.recognition.v1` |
| preset | a named configuration: an engine, its options and a model | `kraken-ppocrv6-medium` |

You only ever pick a preset. The preset says which engine runs and which model it loads, so a run names exactly
what it ran.

An engine works on one **unit**: a line, a region or a whole page. A line recognizer reads lines; a
vision-language model reads pages.

## The catalog

The catalog is the list of everything you can pick. It ships with linecaster as YAML files:

- models and presets,
- recipes,
- normalizations and strategies (see [text and normalization](text.md)),
- rendering policies, conventions and vocabularies.

List the presets with `linecaster presets`. The [catalog pages](../catalog/README.md) describe each entry.

## Engine packages

Engines for kraken, PaddleX, Tesseract and others are separate packages (`linecaster-kraken`, ...), because their
dependencies conflict with each other. The core has no torch and no model runtime. A pipeline script installs
exactly the packages its presets need.

## Recipes

A recipe is a tested combination: one preset for each slot of a pipeline template, plus options such as the texts
to write. `uv run launch.py squiddle scans/ out/` runs the recipe `squiddle`.

## Nothing changes unseen

Each catalog entry has a hash of everything that affects its output. The file `catalog.index` lists the hashes,
so a change of behavior shows up in review. A run record names every entry the run used, with its hash and the
linecaster version. Together they reproduce the run.

## Reference

The [catalog reference](../reference/catalog.md) describes the file formats and the commands.

<!-- docs/concepts/page-records.md -->

# Page records

A page record holds everything a pipeline found on one page, and which component found it.

## Items and pages

An **item** is an ordered set of pages: a book, a newspaper issue, a PDF, a folder of images. A **page** is one
page of an item, with its image.

## What a page record holds

A page record is the page as it goes through a pipeline and as it is stored. Each component adds to it:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    P[page record] --> I[image reference]
    P --> T[transcriptions]
    T --> N["ocr_new: linecaster's own"]
    T --> O["ocr_original: delivered with the page"]
    T --> G["ground_truth: made by people"]
    N --> A[annotations: regions, lines, readings, tables, ...]
    N --> W[annotators: who added them]
```

A **transcription** is everything one source said about the page. A page can have several, side by side.

Each thing a source said is an **annotation**: a region, a line, the reading of a line, a table. An annotation
names its **annotator**: the engine, the preset and the linecaster version that made it. Annotations are added,
never changed.

## Why it is built this way

- You can always see who said what. If two engines disagree, both statements are in the record.
- Nothing is lost. The raw answer of a model is kept next to what was parsed from it.
- One format serves everything: OCR output, a library's delivered OCR and ground truth all use it, so they can be
  compared.

## Where records are stored

A run writes its page records to `OUT/pages/`, as JSON Lines or Parquet. Other pipelines read them from there
with `--pages OUT/pages`.

## Renderings

ALTO, PAGE-XML, hOCR, Markdown, HTML and plain text are written from a page record when you ask for them
(`--files DIR --formats md,alto`). They are **renderings**: outputs, never the stored truth.

## Reference

The [data model](../reference/data-model.md) lists every field. [Serialization](../reference/serialization.md)
describes each output format.

<!-- docs/concepts/text.md -->

# Text and normalization

## The text as read

A page record stores each line's text exactly as the model or the source gave it. Linecaster does not even apply
Unicode normalization to it. This stored text is the **reading**.

The reason is trust. A rule that looks safe can be wrong often. A rule that joins words divided at a line end,
for example, also joins compounds that have a hyphen of their own. A silent change of this kind is an error that
nobody sees.

## Changes are named

Every change of a text has a name and is a catalog entry, a **normalization**:

| Normalization | What it does |
|---|---|
| `nfc` | Unicode NFC |
| `long-s` | writes the long s (ſ) as s |
| `ligatures` | writes ligatures as their letters |
| `flow` | joins the lines of a paragraph into running text |
| `unicode-marks` | removes a hyphen where a word was divided at a line end |

## Strategies

A **strategy** is an ordered list of normalizations. You name one when a text is written:

```bash
--text literal:txt                    # the text as read
--text latin-historic+flow:md         # a catalog strategy, then flow, as Markdown
```

`literal` is the strategy that changes nothing. There is no default strategy that changes text: if you name
none, you get the text as read.

## Scoring uses the same idea

When a run is compared with ground truth, both sides go through the same strategy first, called a **lane**. The
lane `diplomatic` compares the texts almost as they are; `reading` ignores differences a reader would not notice.

## Reference

The [catalog reference](../reference/catalog.md) lists the normalizations and strategies.

<!-- docs/concepts/evaluation.md -->

# Evaluation

Linecaster measures how well a run read its pages by comparing it with ground truth.

## The parts

| Part | What it is |
|---|---|
| ground truth | transcriptions made or checked by people, as page records |
| benchmark | a definition of how to score against one ground truth: which pages, which lanes, which metrics |
| score record | one page's counts for one lane |
| evidence record | the result of scoring one run, with everything needed to compare it with another |

## How scoring works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    G[ground truth files] -->|importer| GR[page records]
    I[page images] -->|pipeline| RR[page records]
    GR --> S[score]
    RR --> S
    B[benchmark] --> S
    S --> E[evidence record]
```

1. An **importer** reads the ground truth (ALTO, PAGE-XML, hOCR, TEI, HTML, plain text) into page records.
2. A pipeline transcribes the same pages.
3. Both sides are rendered the same way and normalized by the same **lane**.
4. The scorer counts character and word errors for the page, and for each region, table and formula on its own.

Rates are computed from counts, so results can be added up across pages without bias.

## What linecaster does not hold

Linecaster ships the scorer and the formats. Ground truths, benchmarks and results are data: they live in the
repository of the evaluation that made them, not in linecaster.

## Reference

[Evaluation](../reference/evaluation.md) defines the lanes, the metrics and the record formats.

<!-- docs/reference/glossary.md -->

# Glossary

The words linecaster uses. Each word has one meaning. A word that needs a second meaning gets a qualifier
("content role", "datatrove `Document`") and is never used bare for it. Code, docs and commit messages use
these terms; a new term is added here before it is used.

The first four sections are the core: what you need to read any other page. The sections after them belong to
one subject each and link to the page that explains it.

## Pipelines

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **component** | One processing unit of a pipeline. Technically a datatrove `PipelineStep` with a contract. Components are named after what they do: `LineRecognizer`, `ParagraphBuilder`, `PageJsonlWriter`. |
| **step** | One kind of work in a pipeline: `layout`, `lines`, `recognition`, `tables`, `formulas`, `image`, `hierarchy`, `paragraphs`, `document`, `import`, `tagging`. An engine does the work of one step and a preset belongs to one step, so the presets of a step are interchangeable. datatrove's class is always written `PipelineStep`. |
| **contract** | What a component reads, adds, replaces and removes in the page record, with its unit and its kind (reader, writer, model, transform, server). Contracts are checked before a run starts. |
| **part** | One named piece of a page record that a contract refers to: `image`, `lines`, `text`, `paragraphs`. The [parts](#parts) table lists them. |
| **unit** | What one call of a component or an engine processes: a `line`, a `region`, a `page` or an `item`. |
| **condition** | A test on the page record. A component with a condition (`when=`) processes only the pages that pass; the others go through unchanged. |
| **composite** | A named group of components that is used like one component, with one contract (`ModularTranscriber`). |
| **pipeline** | An ordered list of components that a stream of pages passes through. A datatrove executor runs it. |
| **pipeline template** | The code that builds one kind of pipeline from options (`linecaster.templates.transcribe_modular`), with an id (`transcribe_modular.v1`). |
| **slot** | A place in a pipeline template that a preset fills. It is named after its step, and so is its flag (`--layout`, `--recognition`). No slot has a default preset. |
| **pipeline script** | A self-contained uv script in `pipelines/` that gives one pipeline template its environment and its command line. |
| **recipe** | A tested way to fill a pipeline template, as a catalog entry: a preset for each slot and the options. |
| **stage** | One datatrove pipeline run as part of a longer computation. Stages run one after another and hand over through files. A pipeline is cut into stages where the unit changes from page to item. |
| **executor**, **job**, **task**, **worker**, **shard** | datatrove's terms. The executor runs a pipeline as tasks. A job is one launch (one HF Job, one Slurm job). A task is one unit of work. Workers are tasks running at the same time. A shard is the part of the input one task reads. |
| **backend** | Where a component's engine runs: in the pipeline's process (`InProcess`), behind `linecaster serve` (`Served`), or behind an OpenAI-compatible server (`Chat`). |
| **server** | A process that hosts models: `linecaster serve`, vLLM or SGLang, or a vendor's own image. The server components `EngineServer`, `VLMServer` and `VendorServer` start one inside a task; they go last in a pipeline. |
| **run** | One execution of a pipeline over one input, into one run folder. |
| **run folder** | The output folder of a run: `pages/` (the page records), `rejects/`, `logs/`, `traces/` and `run.yaml`. |
| **run record** | `run.yaml` in the run folder: the pipeline as it ran, with every component's parameters, the recipe, the command line and the software versions. |
| **sample** | The pages a run reads when it is given a sample rule (`--sample N`). The same input and rule always give the same pages. |
| **reject** | A page that failed a check or a component. It is written to `rejects/` with the reason and stays in the page records with its errors. |
| **error budget** | The share of a task's pages that may fail in a component before the task fails. |
| **warm-up** | What a component loads before its first unit: an engine, a client. |
| **functional parameter**, **operational parameter** | A functional parameter can change what a run writes. An operational parameter only says where things are or how the work runs (folders, ports, worker counts). The run record's hash covers the functional ones. |
| **downstream project** | A project built on linecaster, with its own pipelines, components or engines. Project-specific code lives there, never in linecaster. |

### Parts

| Part | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `image` | The page image's bytes, as the reader brought them. |
| `metadata` | The page record's own fields: ids, sequence, the image's record, the metadata. |
| `transcription_file` | A transcription delivered with the page as a file (ALTO, PAGE-XML, hOCR or text). The `TranscriptionConverter` reads it into a transcription. |
| `regions`, `reading_order`, `lines`, `baselines`, `text`, `words`, ... | What presets produce (`PRODUCES` in the catalog's schema). |
| `line_regions` | Lines assigned to the layout regions and ordered within them (`LineAssigner`). |
| `hierarchy` | Heading levels, headline splits and drop capitals (`HierarchyDetector`). |
| `paragraphs` | The paragraphs of the rows, with the decisions that made them (`ParagraphBuilder`). Structure only, no text. |
| `tags` | Tags with their basis (`Tagger`). |
| `document` | The document of a page or an item (`DocumentBuilder`). It travels with the page through the pipeline and is not stored in the page record. |

## Models and the catalog

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **model** | Weights from upstream (or learned data such as hyphenation patterns), pinned to a revision. |
| **engine** | Code that does the work of one step: it loads a model and processes one unit per call. Engines have a versioned id (`kraken.recognition.v1`). Rule-based engines need no model. Built-in engines are in the core; engine packages (`linecaster-kraken`, ...) add more. |
| **preset** | A named configuration of one engine: its options and the model it loads. A preset is what you pick for a step (`--recognition kraken-ppocrv6-medium`). |
| **catalog** | linecaster's register of models, presets, recipes, normalizations, strategies, rendering policies, conventions and vocabularies. It holds no measurements. |
| **catalog entry** | One thing in the catalog: a YAML file, with an optional Markdown file for prose. |
| **revision** | The exact upstream commit a model is pinned to. |
| **code id** | The versioned id of an engine or a pipeline template: `<name>.v<n>`. |
| **index** | `catalog.index`: the hash of every catalog entry. A change in it is a change of behavior. |

## Pages, items and text

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **item** | A named, ordered container of pages: a book, an issue, a PDF, a folder of images. linecaster assumes nothing more about it. |
| **page** | One page of an item, with its image and its annotation sets. |
| **page record** | A page as stored and as passed through a pipeline (`Page`): the image reference, the annotation sets and the metadata. Components read it and add to it. |
| **item record** | An item with its pages in order, as the `ItemAssembler` passes it on. |
| **page image** | The image a page's coordinates refer to (`PageImage`). |
| **annotation** | One thing an annotator said about a page: a zone, a reading, a table, a formula, a classification, an edit, a link, a reading order. Never changed after it is added. |
| **annotation set** | Everything one source said about one page (`AnnotationSet`). |
| **transcription** | An annotation set that also holds text (`Transcription`). A page has named transcriptions: `ocr_new` (linecaster's), `ocr_original` (delivered with the page), `ground_truth`. |
| **annotator** | Who or what added annotations (`Annotator`): a model, a rule-based engine, a delivered file, or people. It records the engine, the preset, the recipe and the linecaster version. |
| **raw output** | What one request returned, verbatim (`RawOutput`): a model's completion or an engine's native result. |
| **zone** | A place on the page image (`Zone`): a region or a line, with a box and a polygon. |
| **region** | A zone found by layout analysis. |
| **line** | One printed or written line (`Line`): a zone and, once recognized, its reading. |
| **reading** | The text a recognizer read on one line (`Reading`), with its words and alternatives. Stored exactly as given. |
| **reading order** | The order in which a page's regions and lines are read. |
| **row** | The lines of one region that sit side by side at the same height. Detection often splits one printed line into several lines of one row. |
| **classification** | A value of one scheme given to a target (`Classification`): content role, production, heading level, language, script. |
| **content role** | What a region or line is: paragraph, heading, marginalia, footnote, header, page number. Always written with "content". |
| **region label** | The coarser word layout models use for a region (`text`, `title`, `table`, `picture`). Each content role maps to one. |
| **edit** | Another form of a target's text that the source itself states (`Edit`): corrected, expanded, regularized, or the whole of a divided word. The original text stays. |
| **paragraph** | Running text built from the rows of lines (`Paragraph`), with the decisions that made it. |
| **document** | The reader-facing result for a page or an item (`linecaster.document.Document`): titles, headings, paragraphs, tables and notes in order. Built from transcriptions, written as HTML, Markdown, text or JSON. datatrove's class of the same name is always written "datatrove `Document`". |
| **block** | One unit of a document (`Block`): a heading, a paragraph, a list item, a caption, a table, a picture. |
| **rendering** | Anything written from an annotation set: a document, ALTO, PAGE-XML, hOCR, a IIIF annotation page, a text. Renderings are written out and never stored in the page record. |
| **rendering policy** | A catalog entry that decides which annotations go into which layer of a rendering. It changes no text. |
| **layer** | Where a rendering puts content: `body`, `furniture` (running heads, page numbers), `notes`, `background`, `invisible`, `metadata` or `none`. |
| **normalization** | One named change of a text, as a catalog entry: `nfc`, `long-s`, `flow`. Nothing is normalized unless a strategy says so. |
| **strategy** | A named, ordered list of normalizations, as a catalog entry (`latin-historic`). It is applied when a text is written (`--text latin-historic:md`), never to what is stored. Several joined by `+` make an unnamed one (`nfc+long-s+flow`). |
| **per-script engine** | The engine that a by-script engine sends a script's decisions to: a preset of the same step (`by_script`). Its option is named `strategies`; a bare "strategy" is the catalog's. |
| **literal** | The strategy that changes nothing: the readings exactly as given. |
| **text** | A written text of a page or an item: a strategy and a format (`literal:txt`). |
| **flow** | The normalization that joins the rows of a block into running text. A division mark that nothing resolved is kept. |
| **division mark** | A hyphen the typesetter added where a word was divided at a line end. |
| **script** | A writing system, by its ISO 15924 code (`Latn`, `Hebr`). A uv script is always a "pipeline script" or "recipe script". |

## Evaluation

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **ground truth** | A transcription made or checked by people, which runs are scored against. |
| **benchmark** | A definition of how runs are scored against one ground truth: the dataset, the pages, the rendering policy, the lanes and the metrics. |
| **evaluation** | Runs scored under a benchmark, with their score records and evidence records. An evaluation lives in its own repository. |
| **score record** | One page's counts for one text and one lane. Every rate is derived from the counts. |
| **evidence record** | A measurement of a preset or recipe with its source: the run, the benchmark and the scoring it was measured with. Kept by an evaluation, never in the catalog. |
| **element** | A part of a page that is scored on its own: a region's text, a table or a formula. |
| **match group** | Elements of the ground truth and of the output that were matched to each other and are compared as wholes. |
| **lane** | A strategy both sides of a comparison go through before they are counted (`diplomatic`, `reading`, `alnum`). |
| **stratum** | The pages or elements that share one value of a dimension (content role, language, script, a tag). Rates are reported per stratum. |
| **slice** | The pages of a benchmark whose ground truth has tables, formulas, or neither, with rates of their own. |
| **split** | A named share of a ground truth's items (`test`, `train`). Every page of an item is in the same split. |
| **export** | A ground truth and a run written as another project's benchmark files (`linecaster export omnidocbench`). |

## Running at scale

Explained in [pipelines](pipelines.md).

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **item shard** | A folder of page records that holds every page of a set of items, so that a later stage reads whole items. |
| **observer** | A callback before and after each unit of a component: progress, taps, tracing. |
| **tap** | An observer that writes the page records as they leave a given component (`--tap-after`). |
| **partial run** | A run of part of a pipeline: up to a component (`--until`) or from the page records after one (`--after`). |
| **item rank**, **page rank** | An item's place in the sample order, and a page's place within its item. Both come from a hash of the seed and the ids. |
| **stratified sample** | A sample whose pages are chosen separately for each stratum. |
| **secret reference** | `EnvVar("NAME")`: a credential named by its environment variable. It is read in the task and never stored. |
| **image warning** | A fault in an image file that is read around and recorded, without failing the page: for example an optional PNG chunk with a wrong checksum, or EXIF that cannot be read. |
| **working image** | The image preset `working-image`: lossless WebP at full resolution, 8-bit sRGB. |
| **manifest** | An item's list of its pages and their files: a IIIF Presentation manifest or a METS document. |
| **resource** | A remote file of an item or a page (a catalogue record, a manifest, OCR, an image), fetched and kept as a raw copy with a fetch record. |

## Vision-language models

Explained in the [catalog](catalog.md#engines).

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **pass** | One request for a page. A page has more than one pass only when it is repaired. |
| **repair pass** | A further request for a page whose completion stopped at its token limit, with a higher limit. The page keeps the first completion that finished. |
| **repetition detection** | vLLM's guard against a completion that loops: the server ends it early. Such a page is not repaired. |
| **grounding** | A model's mode that labels and locates every text block of the page while it transcribes it. linecaster makes one region per block. |
| **adapter** | The code that talks to one VLM family over the OpenAI-compatible API: its request and its parsing (`linecaster.engines.chat`). |
| **page engine** | An engine whose unit is the page: it reads the whole page and returns its transcription (`PageRecognizer` runs it). |
| **service** | The server a page engine talks to that is neither `linecaster serve` nor a chat server: a vendor's own image. `VendorServer` starts it. |

## Ground-truth sources

Explained in the [catalog](catalog.md) and in [evaluation](evaluation.md).

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **importer** | An engine of the `import` step: it reads a source file into a transcription. |
| **source file** | The file, record or wiki page an importer reads (`SourceFile`). |
| **conventions** | A catalog entry that says what one public source's markup means, as rules an importer applies. |
| **match** | Where a conventions rule points: a CSS selector, a JSONPath or a regular expression. |
| **decision** | What a conventions rule says the matched thing is: `remove`, `text_block`, `note`, `edit`, `cell`. Also: one choice the `ParagraphBuilder` made at a row end, always written "paragraph decision". |
| **coverage** | What an importer's conventions handled on a page: the matches per rule and what no rule matched. |
| **anchor** | Where a zone's text comes from in the source text: a character range. |
| **line image** | An image of one line with its text, as line-level ground-truth datasets give them. |
| **tokenizer** | How the word metrics cut a text into words (`uax29`, `whitespace`, `characters`). A model's tokenizer is always written "the model's tokenizer". |

## Classification schemes

Explained in the [data model](data-model.md).

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **vocabulary** | A catalog entry that defines the values of one classification scheme. |
| **property scheme** | A classification scheme whose values are `yes` and `no`: `degraded`, `tiny`, `rotated`, `multi_column`, `form`. |
| **tag** | A classification in a property scheme, with its basis. No tag does not mean `no`. |
| **tagger** | An engine of the `tagging` step: rules on geometry, or a panel of models. |
| **production** | How content was made: printed, typewritten, handwritten, stamped, born digital. |
| **writing direction** | The direction a page or block is written in: `horizontal-lr`, `horizontal-rl`, `vertical-rl`, `vertical-lr`. |
| **motivation** | Why an annotation was made (`segmenting`, `transcribing`, `classifying`, ...). The W3C Web Annotation term. |
| **shape** | Geometry without an annotator of its own (`Shape`): a word, a glyph, a cell. |
| **word**, **glyph** | A word of a reading, and one character of a word, each with its box and confidence. |
| **link** | A cross-reference between two annotations (`Link`): caption of, note of, continues. |
| **range** | A logical unit of content across pages (`Range`): a chapter, a section, an article. |
| **reference** | A string naming an annotation in the same set (`Ref`). |
| **measurements** | Numbers an annotator records for a page: seconds, tokens, device. |
| **XY-cut**, **XY-Cut++** | The two ways linecaster computes a reading order when the layout model gives none. |
| **cross-layout region** | A text region that spans several columns: longer than 1.3 times the median region and overlapping two or more others horizontally. XY-Cut++ sets it aside before cutting. |

## Fetching

Explained in [HTTP](http.md) and [broker](broker.md).

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **HTTP policy** | How a run's requests go out, from one YAML file (`--http-policy`): rate limits, retries, the User-Agent, the proxies, and a host entry for each host that differs. |
| **host entry** | The settings of one host in an HTTP policy. They replace the general ones. |
| **HTTP block** | A host turning a request away because of where it comes from: a 429 by default (`block_on`). The proxy is left out for that host, or the worker's requests to it pause. An HTTP block does not count as a failed attempt. Always written with "HTTP" or of a proxy or host; a bare "block" is a document's. |
| **unexpected HTML** | A successful response with an HTML page where an image, XML or JSON was expected. A failed attempt by default. |
| **pause** | A time in which a worker sends no request to a host and its requests wait. |
| **breaker** | A guard against an outage: when most recent attempts got a server error, requests pause until the host answers again. |
| **broken proxy** | A proxy that failed several attempts in a row itself. It is left out for every host for a while. |
| **proxies per worker** | How many proxies of a list one worker holds at a time. |
| **broker** | A shared folder through which workers on any machine agree on who uses which shared thing, such as a proxy. It has no server. |
| **lease** | A worker's claim on one thing in the broker. It expires unless renewed. |
| **mark** | A note in the broker that something is unavailable until a time. |
| **worker identity** | Who holds leases in the broker: a numbered place on a machine, which outlives the processes that fill it. |

## Tracing

Explained in [tracing](tracing.md).

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **trace**, **span** | OpenTelemetry's terms. A trace is one page's or one task's path through a run, made of spans. |
| **traced pages** | The pages that get a trace: a fixed share chosen by page id (`--trace-share`), plus every page that failed. |
| **trace context** | A page's `traceparent`, given by the reader. The page's spans are its children. |
| **task span** | A span of the task's own work: a warm-up, a server start, a writer's flush. |
| **gap** | The time a component had no page in it between its first page and its last. |

## Contributing

Explained in [conventions](conventions.md) and [compatibility](compatibility.md).

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **engine API** | What an engine package may import from linecaster besides the data model: `linecaster.engines.api`. |
| **fake engine** | A deterministic CPU engine for tests, one per step (`linecaster.testing`). |
| **conformance check** | `check_engine` and `check_component`: the tests every engine and every component must pass. |
| **generated docs** | The pages `linecaster docs` writes from code, docstrings and the catalog. Never edited by hand and not in git. |
| **breaking change** | A change after which code, a command line, a stored file or a catalog reference stops working or means something else. |
| **upgrade note** | The CHANGELOG entry for a breaking change: what changed, who is affected, what to do. |

## The name

A linecaster is a hot-metal typesetting machine that casts whole lines of type. linecaster makes a new, digital
edition of a printed item, line by line.

<!-- docs/reference/conventions.md -->

# Conventions

Rules that hold across the repository. Each rule is followed by its reason. Terms are the
[glossary](glossary.md)'s.

## Names

| What | Pattern | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| component | `<Object><RoleNoun>`; readers and writers `<Object><Format>Reader` / `Writer` | `LineRecognizer`, `HierarchyDetector`, `DocumentComposer`, `ItemAssembler`, `ManifestReader`, `PageJsonlWriter` |
| composite component | `<Purpose><RoleNoun>` | `ModularTranscriber` |
| component base classes | `<Kind>Component` | `PageComponent`, `ModelComponent`, `RuleComponent` |
| engine class | `<Provider><Step>Engine` | `KrakenRecognitionEngine`, `UnicodeParagraphsEngine` |
| engine id | `<provider>.<step>.v<n>` | `kraken.recognition.v1`, `paragraphs.unicode.v1` |
| VLM adapter | `<Model>Adapter` | `ChandraOCRAdapter` |
| pipeline script | a verb, `<verb>[_<kind>].py` | `harvest.py`, `transcribe_modular.py`, `transcribe_vlm.py`, `transcribe_page.py`, `bind.py` |
| pipeline id | the script's file name, `.v<n>` | `transcribe_modular.v1` |
| slot and its flag | the step's name | `--layout`, `--lines`, `--recognition` |
| step | a noun for what the step produces or does | `layout`, `lines`, `recognition`, `paragraphs`, `document` |
| component package | the step's name, or the plural of what the components are | `linecaster.components.layout`, `linecaster.components.readers` |
| component module | the class's name in snake case | `line_recognizer.py` |
| transcription names | `ocr_new`, `ocr_original`, `ground_truth`, or `<source>` | |

Reason: one pattern makes names guessable, and role nouns say what a component is in a pipeline. Pipeline scripts are
verbs because they are what one runs.

## Words

- Use the [glossary](glossary.md)'s terms. A word has one meaning; a second meaning needs a qualifier ("content
  role", "HTTP block", "datatrove `Document`"). `tests/test_vocabulary.py` keeps retired terms out and checks that
  the glossary defines each term once. Reason: a reader who has learned a word once must be able to rely on it.

## Prose

These hold for the docs, docstrings and help texts.

- Define a term where it first appears on a page, or link it to the glossary.
- One idea per sentence. No parentheses inside parentheses.
- Show an example before the rules that explain it.
- Say what something is and does. Say what it is not only where a reader would otherwise mix two things up.
- Concept pages (`docs/concepts/`) and tutorials (`docs/start/`) explain; reference pages (`docs/reference/`) are
  complete. Neither holds history or measurements: those are in `CHANGELOG.md` and `NOTES.md`.

Reason: the reference grew by adding qualifications to sentences, and became hard to read even for people who
know the subject.

## Spelling

American English everywhere: code, flags, docs, commit messages (normalize, recognizer, behavior, license, color,
catalog). Upstream text copied verbatim (model cards) keeps its spelling.

Reason: one spelling for everything typed, matching Python and its ecosystem.

## YAML and Markdown

- Data that tools read is YAML; prose for people is Markdown. A catalog entry is `<id>.yaml`, optionally with
  `<id>.md` next to it; tools never read the Markdown. Reason: Markdown renders cleanly, data validates, and diffs
  of the two do not mix.
- Every YAML file names its format twice: a first line `# yaml-language-server: $schema=<relative path to
  src/linecaster/catalog/schemas/<kind>-<n>.json>` (editors validate and complete) and a field
  `schema: linecaster.<kind>/<n>` (tools check it). Reason: mistakes show while editing, not at run time.
- The schemas are generated from the pydantic models (`model_json_schema()`) into `src/linecaster/catalog/schemas/`
  (shipped with the package; `linecaster catalog schemas` rewrites them), and a test fails when a committed schema
  differs from a fresh one. The pydantic models are the only source of truth. Reason: one definition, used by
  tools and editors alike.
- YAML is YAML 1.2, read with `ruamel.yaml`: `true`/`false` are the only booleans (`NO` stays a string), duplicate
  keys are errors, and tools that write files back keep their comments.
- An entry's hash covers its functional content (what changes behavior: step, engine, options, pins, settings,
  labels, serving), read from the YAML; `catalog.index` lists every hash, so a change of behavior shows in review and
  goes into the CHANGELOG's Changed outputs. The Markdown prose and descriptive fields (support, provenance) are not
  part of it; git keeps their history.

Schemas: the catalog's kinds without a version (`preset`, `recipe`, `model`, `policy`, `conventions`,
`normalization`, `strategy`: the release versions them), the data formats with theirs (`benchmark-2`, `evidence-3`,
and the older evidence formats readers upgrade, `run-record-2`, `page-6`, `document-2`). Stored page records name
their format in a `schema` field of their row (`linecaster.page/6`).

## Docstrings

Google style, checked by `tests/test_docstrings.py` (with `ast`, no extra tool) for every public component, built-in
engine, backend, serializer, `build`, `run_pages`, `runtime.run.main`, public function of `linecaster.catalog` and
public name of `linecaster.engines.api` and `linecaster.testing`:

- **Summary line**: what the component or function does, in the present tense, starting with a verb, one sentence:
  "Recognizes the text of every line with its engine." It may wrap; it ends at the first blank line. The component
  index and the README's component table show it.
- **Body**: the contract in words (what it reads, adds and replaces), edge cases, what it records (annotators,
  stats, errors on the page).
- **`Args:`** names every parameter of the signature (a class documents its constructor's), and no other: one entry
  each, `name: meaning, the effect of the default, constraints.`, continuation lines indented. Several parameters
  may share an entry (`data_folder, paths_file, ...: datatrove's BaseDiskReader arguments.`), as datatrove's
  inherited reader and writer arguments do; `**kwargs` is an entry too. A class that keeps its base's constructor
  keeps its base's `Args:`.
- **`Example:`** (indented Python code) is required for `runtime.run.main`, `build()`, the serializers (`to_alto`,
  `from_alto`, ...) and the public functions of `linecaster.catalog`; optional for components, whose generated pages show
  it.
- Inline code in double or single backticks; the generated pages render both as code. Engine options are described
  in their `Options` model (`Field(description=...)`), not in a docstring.

Reason: the generated component pages come from the docstrings, so the reference is only as good as they
are, and a test keeps them complete as signatures change.

## Contracts

- Every component declares its unit and what it reads, adds and replaces ([pipelines](pipelines.md)). A part of the
  record is added by one component only, unless a later component declares that it replaces it. Reason: the builder can then
  check a pipeline before it runs and derive its graph.
- Components are pure transforms of their unit; only readers and writers know about tasks, ranks and files. Reason:
  the same components run on any executor and in `run_pages()`.

## Tests

- Every built-in engine passes `linecaster.testing.check_engine` and every public component `check_component`
  (`tests/testing/test_conformance.py`); an engine package checks its engines the same way in
  `engines/<engine>/tests/`. Reason: the protocol and the contracts hold for every implementation, not only the
  ones a pipeline happens to run.
- A test that needs a CUDA device is marked `gpu`, one that downloads weights or reaches the internet `network`, one
  over about 10 s `slow` (`--strict-markers`). Reason: the default
  run skips what a machine cannot run, and CI runs what a CPU can.
- Tests use the fake engines, the fake chat server and the fake service of `linecaster.testing`, not copies of their
  own. Reason: one fake per step behaves the same in every test.

## Tracing

- Tracing (OpenTelemetry) is always on. Spans per task always; spans per page for a trace sample chosen by page id, plus
  every page that failed. Reason: where a run loses time is only visible per page and across processes.
- A page carries its trace context from the reader on; components open spans as children of the page's context, never
  of "the current span". Reason: pages are interleaved in the stream.
- Attributes are identifiers and numbers under `linecaster.*`, never content (text, images). Reason: content
  belongs in the rows, which the page id links to.
- Traces are written to `OUT/traces/` and, when the standard `OTEL_*` variables are set, exported to a backend
  ([tracing](tracing.md)).

## Telemetry

linecaster sends nothing to anyone that the user did not configure. No usage data, no phoning home, not even
opt-in. Reason: libraries and archives run it on their own infrastructure under their own rules.

## Logging

loguru (datatrove's), with `{placeholder}` templates and named values, never formatted strings:
`logger.warning("page {page_id} failed in {component}: {error}", page_id=..., component=..., error=...)` (the values land in
the record's `extra`). JSON lines on Jobs: the pipeline scripts set `LINECASTER_LOG_JSON=1` in their Jobs, where the
tasks (`linecaster.execution.jobs.JobsExecutor`) and `linecaster serve` log with loguru's `serialize=True`
(`linecaster.execution.logs`). Log records carry `trace_id` and `span_id`. Reason: logs can be filtered and joined to
traces.

## Errors

Library code raises the classes of `linecaster.errors` (`PipelineConfigError`, `CatalogError`, `PageError`,
`ServerError`, all `LinecasterError`), never `SystemExit`; only the command line (`linecaster`, a pipeline script's
`main`) turns them into exit codes, and a test fails on any other exit. Pure functions of the data model, the formats
and the text transforms keep Python's own `ValueError` for a wrong argument. Reason: a downstream project that embeds
linecaster can catch what went wrong, and a run's exit code says whether anything was launched.

## Secrets

A credential is never a value in a pipeline: it is an `EnvVar("NAME")` (`linecaster.secrets`), read in the
task. Reason: datatrove pickles the pipeline for every executor, and the run record lists every component's parameters.

## Changes

`CHANGELOG.md` in the Keep a Changelog format, with upgrade notes first. `NOTES.md` is the log of measurements and
decisions; reference documents (`docs/reference/`) describe what is, without history.

<!-- docs/reference/architecture.md -->

# Architecture

What linecaster is made of and how a run fits together. Terms are the [glossary](glossary.md)'s; contracts, the
builder, failures and the run record are in [pipelines](pipelines.md), models, presets, recipes and engines in the
[catalog](catalog.md), the page record in the [data model](data-model.md).

## What linecaster is

An open, modular text-recognition suite for print and handwriting (OCR and HTR, old and new documents). It
combines layout, line, text, table and formula recognizers with rule-based steps (hierarchy, paragraphs,
document) into reproducible datatrove pipelines that turn page images into text: the text as read, texts written
by the transcription strategies a run names (normalized, flowed, dehyphenated only where a strategy says so), ALTO,
PAGE-XML and hOCR on request. It also reads ground truth in any format into the same
data model, writes it as page records and scores runs against it. It is a generalist tool: built on protocols (HTTP,
S3/fsspec, OAI-PMH, IIIF), formats (ALTO, PAGE-XML, hOCR, HTML, Parquet, JSON Lines) and standards (METS/MODS,
Unicode, CSS selectors, JSONPath), its code depends on no collection, site, institution or project; what a public
source's markup means is declarative data in its catalog (conventions). Everything that produces text from images,
and that reads, prepares and scores ground truth, lives here; evaluations and project pipelines (downstream projects) are
built on top of it.

## Packages

| Package | Holds |
|---|---|
| `linecaster.data` | the data model: `Item`, `Page`, `PageImage`, annotation sets (`AnnotationSet`, `Transcription`) with their annotators (`Annotator`), raw outputs (`RawOutput`) and annotations, `Text`, rendering policies (`RenderingPolicy`), the measurements vocabulary |
| `linecaster.formats` | ALTO, PAGE-XML and hOCR out and in; HTML in (`HtmlConverter`, by HTML's semantics and a source's conventions); plain text in; DoclingDocuments in (the `docling` extra); the IIIF annotation page |
| `linecaster.document` | a page's or an item's document (`Document`, its blocks and their origins), built from transcriptions (`DocumentBuilder`) and written as HTML, Markdown, text and JSON |
| `linecaster.conventions` | conventions: their format (`linecaster.conventions`), layering, decisions, matchers (CSS selectors, JSONPath, regular expressions), coverage, and anchors into a source text by alignment |
| `linecaster.normalization` | the normalizations' rules on characters, LaTeX as text |
| `linecaster.text` | pure functions on text and on transcriptions: the rules of the hierarchy and paragraphs steps (`hierarchy`, `paragraphs`), scripts and writing directions, offsets through a change of text, a page's literal text |
| `linecaster.images` | the working image, plots |
| `linecaster.engines` | the engine API (`linecaster.engines.api`) and the built-in engines: the rule-based steps (`hierarchy`, `paragraphs`, `document`, `image`), the importers, the taggers and the single-region layout |
| `linecaster.core` | what every component builds on: `Component`, `PageComponent`, `ModelComponent`, `RuleComponent`, contracts, composites |
| `linecaster.components` | the components, one package per step or kind ([components](../components/README.md)) |
| `linecaster.backends` | `InProcess`, `Served`, `Chat` |
| `linecaster.engines.chat` | one adapter per VLM family, `ADAPTERS` |
| `linecaster.evaluation` | the scorer: lanes, metrics, elements, benchmarks, evidence records, ground-truth tools |
| `linecaster.serving` | `linecaster serve` |
| `linecaster.net` | http(s) fetching (`linecaster.net.http`), the HTTP policy, the proxy pools ([http](http.md)) |
| `linecaster.net.broker` | the [broker](broker.md): leases, marks and worker slots in a shared folder; `linecaster broker` |
| `linecaster.pipeline` | `Pipeline`: a list of components checked, run and recorded as one |
| `linecaster.execution` | the builder, the pipelines' command line (`options`, `wiring`, `allocation`, `run`), executors, the run record, Jobs helpers, logs |
| `linecaster.templates` | the pipeline templates, one per pipeline script ([pipelines](pipelines.md#pipeline-templates)) |
| `linecaster.catalog` | the catalog: its entries (normalizations and strategies among them), their schemas, the index, fetching pins |
| `linecaster.schemas` | every format by its schema id, and the JSON Schemas written from them |
| `linecaster.secrets` | `EnvVar`: a credential named by its environment variable |
| `linecaster.tracing` | tracing (OpenTelemetry) and `linecaster traces` |
| `linecaster.docs` | `linecaster docs`: the generated pages of the components and the catalog |
| `linecaster.testing` | test helpers: sample pages, fake engines (`fake.<step>.v1`, the page engine `fake.recognition.page.v1`), a fake chat server, a fake HTTP service, the conformance checks `check_engine` and `check_component`, the pytest markers |

The packages are layers, and a module imports at its top only from its own layer or below
(`tests/test_import_rule.py`):

`errors`, `secrets` ← `data` ← `text`, `normalization`, `conventions`, `images` ← `formats` ← `document` ←
`engines` ← `catalog` ← `evaluation` ← `net`, `backends` ← `core` ← `tracing` ← `components` ← `serving` ←
`execution`, `pipeline` ← `templates` ← `schemas`, `docs`, `testing`, `cli`

An import inside a function may reach up: the builder puts writers into a pipeline, and the catalog asks which
engines are installed.

`linecaster.data`, `formats`, `document`, `conventions`, `normalization`, `text`, `images`, `engines` and
`evaluation` load neither datatrove nor saturate, nor linecaster's components or runtime (`tests/test_import_rule.py`),
so downstream projects can use the data model and the formats without the pipeline machinery. datatrove and saturate are
required dependencies, datatrove with its `io` and `s3` extras (`s3://` paths work everywhere), and so is httpx
(`http(s)://` through `linecaster.net`); engines, Ray and PDFium are not (engine packages and extras).

## Components and backends

A component is a datatrove `PipelineStep` with a contract; a pipeline is a list of components run by a datatrove executor.
Each step or kind of component has a subpackage of `linecaster.components` ([components](../components/README.md) has a page per component).

**Model components** (`ModelComponent`: `LayoutDetector`, `LineDetector`, `LineRecognizer`, `TableRecognizer`,
`FormulaRecognizer`, `PageRecognizer`, `RegionRecognizer`) each have a backend:

- `InProcess("pkg:Class", **kwargs)` (or a preset ref) loads the engine in the worker, in `warm_up()` before the
  first page; a loaded engine is never pickled. In-process is always available and is the parity reference.
- `Served(endpoint, model=name)` and `Chat(preset, endpoint)` (a VLM) stream pages through saturate
  (`AdaptiveClient` and `through()`): a window of pages in flight, adapted to the server's queue gauges and 429s;
  results passed on as they finish; secrets as `EnvVar`. The streaming exists once, in `ModelComponent`.

A page that failed a step carries `doc.metadata["errors"]`, passes later model steps at once and goes to
`rejects/`; more failures than the error budget fail the task ([pipelines](pipelines.md#failures)). Library code
raises `linecaster.errors`, never `SystemExit`.

**Rule components** (`RuleComponent`: `HierarchyDetector`, `ParagraphBuilder`, `DocumentComposer`; and `ImageConverter`)
run a built-in engine of a rule-based step in the pipeline's process, picked by a preset.

## One page per request

A request carries one page; engines batch only within a page (kraken batches a page's lines). A page's result
depends only on the page, never on what else is in flight, so runs are deterministic whatever the executor, the
number of tasks or the backend.

## Servers

- **`linecaster serve`** hosts engines: stateless (no state between requests), one worker per model (several
  replicas per model were measured at +7–10 % and removed; NOTES.md), each with a bounded queue (`--max-queue`; a
